title: Pipeline Stage Step-Level Architecture

scope.purpose: Describe the structural contract of a Stage-composable Step, its internal Step Composition, pluggable SPUs, optional supporting units, and their distinct execution results.
scope.appliesTo: Each concrete Step Instance composed by an owning Stage.

step.definition: A Stage-composable processing and orchestration component that exposes its own specialized input/output contract and internally coordinates the SPU Instances and supporting units required for its responsibility.
step.identity: Each Step is defined within the context of its owning Stage and has its own specialized input, output, processing flow, internal component composition, and applicable supporting components.
architecturalNature: Step is the Stage-facing Aggregate Root boundary for its internal composition.
Step provides a Facade to Stage and hides its internal SPU/supporting-unit topology.
Step owns its Step Composition and delegates internal orchestration and Step-specific flow control to that composition.
Step owns the public lifecycle boundary for its Aggregate and is accountable for safe settlement of accepted Step invocations and internal obligations before confirming terminal retirement.
optionalSupportingComponents: Error Handling Units and Operation Entry Publisher
step.compositionConstraint: A Step selects only the SPUs and supporting units required by its responsibility. No fixed number or mandatory supporting-unit set is imposed.
step.stageBoundary: Stage Composition invokes Step through Step[TInput,TOutput] and consumes StepExecutionResult[TOutput]. It does not invoke or coordinate internal SPUs directly. Stage Composition requests retention for reuse or terminal retirement only through the public Step lifecycle boundary and acts on the specialized outcome; it does not coordinate internal shutdown.
step.result: StepExecutionResult[TOutput], returned by the concrete Step and assembled by Step Composition from retained SPUExecutionResult values and applicable supporting-unit results according to the concrete Step specialization.

requiredContractSpecializations.whenApplicable: Every concrete Step using ErrorHandlingUnits and OperationEntryPublisher MUST instantiate all obligations in 01.02_Step_Error_Handling/Single_Step_Publication_Specialization_Contract.json.
mandatoryAreas: Concrete ReservationGrant, PublicationAcknowledgement, PublicationStatus, PublicationRejection, ReleaseAcknowledgement, and PublisherContractViolation representations.
Concrete non-throwing transfer of the complete Step THandlingOperationResult and ErrorHandlingOperationEntry.
Named Step-owned Recovery Owner and recovery procedure for pre-acceptance violations and indeterminate acceptance.
Representation, generation authority, uniqueness scope, stability, retirement, and reuse rules for all publication identities.
Publication-status retention, tombstone, and expiry policy.
End-to-end custody trace through ErrorHandlerResult and StepExecutionResult.
requiredContractSpecializations.completionRule: A Step using this path is not contract-complete until these specializations are concrete and pass the specialization-contract completion gate. Common-contract references alone are insufficient.
requiredContractSpecializations.nonApplicableRule: A Step without this publication path records explicit non-applicability and its architectural reason.

step.compositionBoundary: Step Composition is the authoritative internal coordination responsibility defined by 00.00_Step/Step_Composition_Contract.json. Step owns it; Stage interacts only with Step.

stepProcessingUnit.definition: The actual pluggable processing unit that performs one specialized processing responsibility within its owning Step.

typeParameters.name: TInput
typeParameters.meaning: The input type accepted by the Step Processing Unit.

typeParameters.name: TOutput
typeParameters.meaning: The processing artifact type produced by the Step Processing Unit.

stepProcessingUnit.specialization: Each concrete Step Processing Unit realizes the generic execution contract and specializes its input and output types for its own processing responsibility.
responsibilities: Perform the actual specialized processing assigned to this SPU.
Accept the SPU-specific input supplied by Step Composition.
Return SPUExecutionResult[TOutput] for a normally completed invocation.
Define and register SPU-owned error type definitions through its assigned Registry.
Create SPUError occurrences for errors arising within its own processing responsibility and make them available to Step Composition.

errorOwnershipAndProduction.definitionOwnership: Each concrete SPU owns the specialized SPUErrorTypeDefinition types and definitions for its own error domain.
errorOwnershipAndProduction.registration: The SPU registers its definitions through its assigned SPUErrorTypeDefinitionRegistry. The Pipeline owns and manages the Registry Instance; registration authority does not transfer Registry ownership to the SPU.
errorOwnershipAndProduction.occurrenceCreation: The SPU creates SPUError[TErrorOccurrenceContext] occurrences for errors arising within its own processing responsibility. Each occurrence references exactly one definition registered in that SPU's assigned Registry.
errorOwnershipAndProduction.resultContribution: The SPU provides the occurrences it creates to the Step's ErrorResult construction or aggregation process. The detailed ErrorResult contract and aggregation rules are defined by the Step Error Model.
errorOwnershipAndProduction.exceptionSeparation: A thrown exception that prevents the SPU from returning StepExecutionResult remains distinct from an SPUError occurrence and is not automatically converted into one.

validatorUnits.role: Perform validation responsibilities associated with the Step Processing Unit.
validatorUnits.resultRequirement: Each validator unit provides its own structured result.
validatorUnits.coordinationBoundary: Step Composition selects/associates, provisions, invokes, and retains applicable Validator Unit results according to the concrete Step specialization.
validatorUnits.ownershipBoundary: Validator Units retain their own validation semantics and result contracts. Step Composition owns internal orchestration and lifecycle/reuse decisions; no universal validator-to-SPU cardinality or validation order is imposed.

errorModel.role: Define the Step-specific ErrorResult contract, including the representation semantics and aggregation rules for SPU error occurrences and any other Step error/failure information within the scope of that Step.
errorModel.association: Step-specific; its required contents are defined incrementally for each Step.
responsibilities: Define the structure and semantics of the Step-specific ErrorResult contract.
Define how SPUError occurrences are represented within ErrorResult.
Define the Step-specific aggregation rules for the error information carried by ErrorResult.
Keep error identification/occurrence information distinct from the results of error-handling activities.
Define the occurrence-entry structure that associates each original SPUError occurrence with its producerSPUIdentity.
Require preservation of occurrenceIdentity and the complete SPUErrorTypeDefinitionReference, including registryIdentity and errorTypeIdentity, when occurrences are represented in ErrorResult.
Define how ErrorHandlerResult may refer to handled occurrences by the composite producerSPUIdentity and occurrenceIdentity without containing or merging ErrorResult.
boundaries: The Step Error Model defines ErrorResult structure, representation semantics, and aggregation rules; it need not be a separate runtime object that physically executes aggregation.
SPUs own their SPUErrorTypeDefinition definitions and create occurrences for errors arising within their own processing responsibilities.
Step Composition collects eligible occurrences and performs physical ErrorResult assembly according to the Step Error Model.

The Step Error Model does not own SPUErrorTypeDefinition definitions or the SPUErrorTypeDefinitionRegistry assigned to an SPU; the Pipeline retains the Registry ownership specified by the common Error Model contract.
Occurrence identity, producerSPUIdentity, and the complete SPUErrorTypeDefinitionReference remain preserved as required by the Step Error Model.
ErrorHandlerResult remains independent; references to handled occurrences do not embed or mutate ErrorResult.
errorModel.nature: A Step-specific contract/specification defining ErrorResult structure and aggregation semantics; it is not presumed to be an executable runtime unit.
errorModel.coordinationBoundary: SPUs create their own SPUError occurrences. Step Composition collects eligible occurrences and physically assembles ErrorResult by applying the Step Error Model's rules.

errorHandlingUnits.role: Perform the error-handling responsibilities associated with the Step Processing Unit.
errorHandlingUnits.resultRequirement: Each Error Handling Unit provides a structured, Step-specialized THandlingOperationResult for each operation execution it performs; the applicable Step-specific error-handling composition represents those operation results as entries in ErrorHandlerResult.
responsibilities: Perform the error-handling operations assigned by the owning Step design.
Identify the SPUError occurrences targeted by each operation using the Step-defined composite occurrence reference.
Provide a structured operation-specific result for each operation execution that returns a result.
Accept a Step-specialized input and use only the target-occurrence access authorized for the current invocation.

Produce a distinct operation entry for each handling operation that returns a structured result, preserving unit identity, operation identity, target occurrence references, and operation-specific result.
boundaries: Error Handling Units execute the handling operations assigned by the concrete Step and produce operation-specific results under their own contracts.
Step Composition coordinates Unit association, lifecycle/reuse, invocation, and collection; association with a particular SPU does not transfer those responsibilities to the SPU.

The Step-specific Error Handling Composition owns the OperationEntryPublisher instance/protocol scope assigned to it, accepts/reconciles complete operation entries, and assembles ErrorHandlerResult from accepted entries.
Step Composition coordinates with that Error Handling Composition and integrates its ErrorHandlerResult into StepExecutionResult where applicable.
Operation results do not contain ErrorResult; target references identify occurrences without embedding or mutating the ErrorResult aggregate.
The concrete Step must satisfy Single_Step_Publication_Specialization_Contract.json whenever it uses Error Handling Units and OperationEntryPublisher.
No global Pipeline- or Stage-level Error Handling Unit manager is introduced.
errorHandlingUnits.lifecycleOwnership: The owning Step Composition controls association, provisioning, invocation coordination, collection, reuse, and release of Error Handling Unit instances. A Unit may be associated with a particular SPU, but that association does not transfer orchestration or lifecycle ownership to the SPU.
errorHandlingUnits.coordinationBoundary: Step Composition owns internal association, provisioning/reuse/release decisions, invocation coordination, and result collection for Error Handling Unit instances, including instances associated with a particular SPU. The Step-specific Error Handling Composition owns publication aggregation and ErrorHandlerResult assembly.

observationUnits.role: Provide optional observability capabilities associated with the Step execution, including logging, telemetry, and integrations with observability systems or services where needed.
observationUnits.responsibility: Observe relevant execution events, state, timing, diagnostics, or contextual information and publish or forward observability data through the applicable mechanisms.
observationUnits.resultRequirement: An Observation Unit may define its own result contract if its operation requires one; that contract is independent of StepExecutionResult.
observationUnits.executionResultRelationship: Observation activity and its own results are not fields of StepExecutionResult. StepExecutionResult aggregates the processing artifact and the specified validation, error, and error-handling results only.
observationUnits.coordinationBoundary: Step Composition coordinates applicable Observation Unit association and invocation at the scope and timing selected by the concrete Step.
boundaries: Observation Units own their observation semantics and any event/result contract.
Observation activity and Observation Unit results remain outside StepExecutionResult by default.
Step Composition coordination does not turn observation data into processing output or impose a universal observation-failure policy.
The concrete Step defines any required failure isolation or explicit application-specific integration.

executionResult.name: StepExecutionResult
executionResult.purpose: Provide the Stage-facing structured aggregate result for one complete Step invocation.
executionResult.producer: The concrete Step Instance / Step Composition, not an individual SPU.
inputs: SPUExecutionResult values returned by internal SPU invocations

optionalElements.name: processingArtifact
optionalElements.meaning: The Step-level output artifact exposed to Stage.

optionalElements.name: validatorResult
optionalElements.meaning: The Step-specialized validation result or aggregate.

optionalElements.name: errorResult
optionalElements.meaning: The Step-level ErrorResult defined by its Step Error Model.

optionalElements.name: errorHandlerResult
optionalElements.meaning: The Step-level aggregate of accepted error-handling operation entries.

executionResult.optionality: Each element is independently optional; absence is not itself a status.
executionResult.preservation: Step Composition preserves all required results actually produced and retained, including those produced before a later failure.
executionResult.observationBoundary: Observation data and Observation Unit results remain outside StepExecutionResult.

constraints: Step is distinct from SPU and is the Stage-facing Aggregate Root/Facade boundary.
Stage Composition interacts with Step through the public Step contract and does not bypass it to invoke or coordinate internal SPUs or supporting units.
Step owns its Step Composition; Step Composition owns the Step-specific internal orchestration and flow decisions.
Each SPU performs its assigned processing responsibility and returns SPUExecutionResult for a normally completed invocation; it does not assemble StepExecutionResult.

SPUs create SPUError occurrences for errors arising within their own processing responsibilities; Step Composition collects eligible occurrences and assembles ErrorResult according to the Step Error Model.
The Step Error Model defines ErrorResult semantics and is not presumed to be an executable runtime unit.
Step Composition owns association and lifecycle/reuse coordination for supporting-unit instances, including Error Handling Units associated with particular SPUs.

The Step-specific Error Handling Composition aggregates accepted operation entries into ErrorHandlerResult; Step Composition integrates that independent result into StepExecutionResult where applicable.
Observation Units retain independent observation semantics/results; observation data remains outside StepExecutionResult by default.
Supporting component categories are optional unless a concrete Step specialization makes them applicable or required.
The internal ordering, topology, and response to exceptions are Step-specific and are not prescribed by the common architecture.

Step invocation admission and terminal-retirement admission closure have a well-defined linearizable ordering; accepted invocations are included in settlement and later invocations are not admitted as ordinary work.
Stage Composition distinguishes retention for reuse from terminal retirement and interacts with Step lifecycle only through the public Step boundary.
Step Composition coordinates internal quiescence, result/custody reconciliation, and component release; Stage Composition does not inspect or manage internal components.
An unresolved retirement outcome prevents Step from being treated as terminally released or safely reusable until concrete reconciliation establishes that condition.

references.relationship: Stage-facing Step and Step Composition contract
authoritative internal Step composition and supporting-unit coordination contract
ErrorResult semantics and occurrence aggregation rules
Error Handling Unit execution and lifecycle contract

openDesignDetails: The exact structured result types and composition rules for multiple validator units are not defined here.
The exact error result structure is owned by the Step Error Model and its detailed contract.
The exact Observation Unit interfaces, event model, configuration, and integrations are defined only where required by individual Steps.
The exact execution protocol and validation/processing/error-handling/observation order are defined per Step.
Concrete ErrorHandlerResult type specializations and Error Handling Unit operation-result contracts are defined by the Step-specific error-handling contract.
Each concrete Step must instantiate the mandatory publication specialization when applicable; no cross-Step concrete defaults are supplied.

Concrete Step specializations define the public lifecycle interaction, linearizable execute-admission closure, reuse and terminal-retirement outcomes, and recovery for failed/indeterminate retirement; Step Composition specializations define internal settlement evidence.
